correctness.rationale: The C5 action on the 3-by-5 ordinary rook complex is free because every face contains at most one vertex per row. The source has precisely 15 vertices, 60 edges, 60 triangles, yielding quotient orbit cells (3,12,12). After collapsing a maximal tree the twelve attaching relators are a_i c_{j-i} b_j^{-1}; nine valid free-group generator eliminations leave t^5, t^{-5}, and the empty relator. A two-cell slide gives the precise CW homotopy equivalence to S1 cup_5 e2 wedged with two S2. The universal-cover chain R --N--> R --(g-1)--> R gives ker(N)=I_C5, and each wedge two-sphere contributes the regular R-module, yielding I_C5 plus R^2. Every finite orbit and reduction is independently recomputed from definitions by the embedded Python verifier, but a verifier alone is not used as the proof.

value.rationale: The 3-by-5 board is the smallest stable three-row shellable ordinary chessboard, so its simplest nontrivial column rotation is a natural and motivating symmetry quotient. The result settles its entire two-dimensional homotopy type, detects genuine order-five torsion created in the geometric orbit, and identifies the nontrivial integral deck-lattice I_C5 plus two regular summands on 14-dimensional covering H2. Those details are not consequences of the previously available nonequivariant wedge count or rational character and can be used in integral equivariant calculations.
